status: Full core specification fixtures; not all implemented/executed. Scalar, concrete-product and call-scoped ownership execution evidence is maintained separately.

cases.reason: Explicitly copyable named values preserve the source after assignment and ordinary calls.
Wildcard discard does not move the existing owner; mutable/read access borrows it and a later consuming call transfers ownership.
Unconstrained read, Copy-constrained value, and explicit consuming generic contracts remain distinct.
Loop mutation and branch-complete delayed initialization satisfy the core rules.
Explicit colon results and inferred tails/returns agree; anchored recursion and consuming generic results infer without callers, and Unit values remain Copy.
Explicit/inferred Never results join with returning branches without becoming Unit; explicit wildcard discard has a Unit result on normal completion.
The lowercase spelling is not a predeclared type alias; use Never.
Reachable i32 and bool returns cannot determine one compatible result type.
An unanchored mutually recursive result cannot be inferred from main's expected i32 or defaulted to Unit/Never.
Empty parentheses are the unit value, not a result type; write Unit.
The old arrow result delimiter is rejected; explicit results use a colon.
The tail expression accesses first after its non-copy value moved to second.
A declared read parameter cannot become an owned T; reject even without instantiation.
Wrapper cannot opt into Copy because Counter did not opt in.
An explicit consuming parameter invalidates the caller source even when its type is copyable.
